title: Inside the strongest open models
kicker: Architecture, data, recipes and what matters
blurb: Ten leading open-weights models compared: sparse experts, compressed attention, stability, data, and why post-training seems to decide the score.
description: The best open-weights model scores 46 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v4.3.2) and the best closed model 58. The film compares ten open models: mixture of experts, long-context attention, training stability, data, and reinforcement learning. Its reading is that agentic post-training explains more of the gap than size or token count.
takeaways: Index scores only compare within one version, because the benchmark gets harder with each release.
Nearly every top open model is a sparse mixture of experts, so only a small share of weights is used per token.
Compressed and hybrid attention keep the KV cache manageable at a million tokens of context.
Active parameters and training tokens predict score only weakly across these ten models, while agentic reinforcement learning stands out.
On Arena, which measures human preference, only one open model reaches the top fifteen.
